rationale: The assistant parsed the messy opener well, gave safe unplug-first checks in a sensible order and correctly identified the snapped belt caused by the hair/tassel jam, matching the hidden truth. However it badly over-escalated: despite the customer explicitly saying 'no sparks or electrical smell btw, just the rubber smell when it stopped', it repeated the 'Stop using this appliance' banner and insisted 'do not use the vacuum again or fit a belt and test it yourself. It needs a qualified engineer', when a user-level belt change is appropriate and the ground truth marks electrical-fire-risk engineer referral as unsupported. It also never asked for the model number needed to source the correct belt, nor for the brushbar switch setting, so the homeowner is left with a correct diagnosis but an unnecessary engineer bill and no path to the right part.
